name: Cabinet of Oman
description: Chief executive body of the Sultanate of Oman, officially the Council of Ministers, led by Sultan Haitham bin Tariq in his role as prime minister.

key_people.title: Prime Minister (Chairman of the Council of Ministers)
key_people.name: Sultan Haitham bin Tariq

relationships.target_name: Ministries of the Sultanate of Oman

name: Council of Oman
description: Bicameral parliament of Oman made up of the State Council (upper house) and Majlis A'Shura (lower house), stipulated in Article 58 of the Basic Law of the State; assists the government in drawing up general state policies.

name: State Council (Majlis al-Dawla)
description: Appointed upper house of the Council of Oman, Oman's bicameral parliament.

name: Majlis A'Shura
description: Elected lower house of the Omani Parliament (Council of Oman), established in 1991; members are directly elected, the only chamber of Oman's legislature with popularly elected members.

name: Supreme Judicial Council
description: Government institution responsible for overseeing and managing judicial affairs in the Sultanate of Oman.

name: Supreme Court of Oman
description: Highest court in the Omani judicial system; standardizes legal principles, reviews decisions of lower courts and monitors judges.

name: Ministry of Foreign Affairs
description: Government ministry responsible for Oman's foreign relations and diplomacy.

key_people.title: Foreign Minister
key_people.name: Sayyid Badr bin Hamad bin Hamoud Al Busaidi

name: Ministry of Defence
description: Omani government ministry responsible for military and national defense matters; carries out the defense policy of the Sultan's Armed Forces.

name: Ministry of Interior
description: Government ministry responsible for internal affairs, including regional administration and elections.

name: Ministry of Finance
description: Governmental body responsible for the state budget and public finances of the Sultanate of Oman.

key_people.title: Minister of Finance
key_people.name: Sultan bin Salim bin Said Al Habsi

name: Ministry of Education
description: Governmental body responsible for general (school) education in the Sultanate of Oman.

name: Ministry of Health
description: Government ministry responsible for public health and the national health system of Oman.

name: Ministry of Commerce and Industry
aliases: Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Investment Promotion
description: Government ministry responsible for commerce, industry and investment promotion; the entity's current designation includes investment promotion following 2020 restructuring.

name: Ministry of Energy and Minerals
aliases: Oman Ministry of Energy and Minerals
description: Government ministry responsible for the energy and minerals sectors of Oman.

name: Diwan of Royal Court
subcategory: Royal Household / Head of State Apparatus
description: Senior body of the royal court of the Sultan of Oman, headed by a minister; handles royal court affairs and senior state appointments.

key_people.title: Minister of the Diwan of Royal Court
key_people.name: Sayyid Khalid bin Hilal Al Busaidi

name: Oman Investment Authority
description: Investment arm and sovereign wealth fund of the Sultanate of Oman, established by Royal Decree No. 61/2020; manages state funds and a portfolio of more than 160 state-owned companies, with about US$53 billion in assets under management (2024).

name: Petroleum Development Oman
description: Leading exploration and production company of Oman, delivering the majority of the country's crude oil production and natural gas supply; owned by the Government of Oman (60%), Shell (34%), TotalEnergies (4%) and Partex (2%).

name: OQ
description: Oman's state-owned integrated energy company, formed in 2019 through the merger of Oman Oil Company and Orpic Group.

name: Oman LNG
description: Liquefied natural gas production company established in 1994, operating liquefaction trains at Sur; majority-owned by the Government of Oman with international energy partners.

name: Omantel
description: Oman's incumbent telecommunications operator, majority-owned by the Oman Investment Authority and listed on the Muscat Stock Exchange; subsidiaries include Oman Data Park and Omantel International.

name: Oman Air
description: Flag carrier airline of Oman, based at Muscat International Airport; operates domestic and international passenger services as well as regional air taxi and charter flights.

name: Omran Group
description: State-owned tourism development group of Oman, overseeing a portfolio of hotels, destinations and community-focused development assets.

name: Madayn
description: Public Establishment for Industrial Estates, established in 1993 by Royal Decree No. 32/93; develops and manages industrial cities across the Sultanate of Oman.

name: Asyad Group
description: Oman's state-owned integrated logistics group under the Oman Investment Authority, covering ports, shipping, and third-party logistics; Asyad Shipping Company listed on the Muscat Stock Exchange after a 2025 IPO.

name: Ooredoo Oman
description: Private telecommunications operator in Oman (launched as Nawras in 2004), part of the Ooredoo Group; second mobile operator after Omantel.

name: Awasr
description: Omani fixed broadband (fiber-to-the-home) telecommunications operator founded in 2016.

name: MB Holding
description: Omani private conglomerate established in 1982, active in oil and gas drilling services, mining, engineering and investments.

name: Al Maha Petroleum
aliases: Al Maha Petroleum Products Marketing Company
description: Omani fuel marketing and retail company established in 1993, operating petrol stations across the Sultanate.

name: Oman Charitable Organization
description: Charitable organization established in 1996; state-funded body that supports and finances social care and welfare programs in Oman.

name: Dar al Atta'a
description: Non-profit, volunteer-based charity established in Oman in 2002 by a group of women; provides education support, family welfare, housing aid and relief programs for underprivileged families.

name: Environment Society of Oman
description: Founded in March 2004, the first environmental NGO of its kind in Oman; works to conserve Oman's natural heritage and raise environmental awareness.

name: Oman Chamber of Commerce and Industry
description: Established on 15 May 1973 by royal decree as a private institution of public benefit; organizes and represents the business community, issues certificates of origin and promotes Omani trade and industry.

name: Sultan Qaboos University
description: Oman's national university, established in 1986; the premier public research university of the Sultanate, located in Muscat.

name: University of Nizwa
description: Private university in Nizwa founded in 2002, one of Oman's leading non-profit private universities.

name: Sohar University
description: Private university in Sohar founded in 1998, Oman's first private university.

name: German University of Technology in Oman
description: Private university established in 2007 in Muscat (Halban) in cooperation with RWTH Aachen University, Germany.

name: Dhofar University
description: Private university in Salalah (Dhofar Governorate) established in 2004.

name: University of Technology and Applied Sciences
description: Oman's public applied-technology university system, tracing to 1984, with campuses including Muscat, Ibri and other governorates.

name: Oman TV
description: State television broadcaster of Oman, launched in 1974 and operated under the Ministry of Information; sister channels include Oman TV Sport, Oman TV Cultural and Oman TV Live.

name: Oman News Agency
description: Official state news agency of Oman, established in 1986, providing official news coverage of the Sultanate in Arabic and English.

name: Oman Daily Observer
description: English-language daily newspaper published in Muscat by the Ministry of Information; positions itself as Oman's leading English daily.

name: Times of Oman
description: Daily English-language newspaper based in Muscat; the oldest English-language newspaper of Oman, founded by Essa bin Mohammed Al Zedjali.

name: Alwatan
description: Arabic-language daily newspaper in Oman, among the country's oldest Arabic dailies.

name: Al Shabiba
description: Leading Arabic-language daily newspaper based in Muscat, published by Muscat Media Group; known for strong appeal to younger readers.

name: Central Bank of Oman
description: Central bank of Oman, established in December 1974 and operational from 1 April 1975, replacing the Oman Currency Board as principal currency authority; licenses and supervises all banks operating in Oman.

key_people.title: Chairman of the Board of Directors
key_people.name: Taimur bin Asa'ad Al Said

name: BankMuscat
description: Oman's largest bank by assets, established in 1982 and headquartered in Muscat; listed on the Muscat Stock Exchange.

name: National Bank of Oman
description: Founded in 1973, the National Bank of Oman was the first local bank in Oman; listed on the Muscat Stock Exchange.

name: Bank Dhofar
description: Commercial bank in Oman headquartered in Salalah/Muscat, listed on the Muscat Stock Exchange; ranked among Oman's largest banks.

name: Oman Arab Bank
description: One of Oman's leading financial institutions with a legacy dating back to 1973 and formal establishment in 1984.

name: Alizz Islamic Bank
description: Islamic bank of Oman offering Sharia-compliant retail and corporate banking.

name: Sohar International
description: One of Oman's largest domestic banks (Sohar International Bank SAOG), licensed by the Central Bank of Oman; grew significantly after combining with HSBC Oman's local operations.

name: Bank Nizwa
description: Omani Islamic bank licensed by the Central Bank of Oman, among the leading full-fledged Islamic banks in the Sultanate.

name: Muscat Stock Exchange
description: Principal stock exchange of Oman, located in Muscat; formerly known as the Muscat Securities Market (MSM), key listed sectors include banking, energy and telecoms.

name: Sultan's Armed Forces
aliases: Armed Forces of the Sultanate of Oman
description: Combined armed forces of Oman, tracing founding to 1907; comprise the Royal Army of Oman, Royal Air Force of Oman and Royal Navy of Oman, under the Ministry of Defence.

name: Royal Army of Oman
description: Ground forces component of the Sultan of Oman's Armed Forces, founded in 1907 as the Muscat Garrison; the largest service branch.

name: Royal Air Force of Oman
description: Air warfare branch of Oman's military, operating under the Sultan's Armed Forces.

name: Royal Navy of Oman
description: Naval warfare branch of the Royal Armed Forces of the Sultanate of Oman.

name: Royal Guard of Oman
description: Personal security and ceremonial unit responsible for the protection of the Sultan of Oman and the Royal Family.

name: Royal Oman Police
description: Main law and order agency for the Sultanate of Oman, covering policing, customs and civil defence functions; headed by the Inspector-General of Police and Customs.

name: Internal Security Service
description: Principal domestic intelligence and security agency of the Sultanate of Oman.
